text:
The glass is cold against my cheekbone’s ridge,
A frame of frost for the electric sprawl.
The city hums its low, metallic bridge,
And lights cascade like rain within a hall.

I watch the windows flicker, pass, and die,
Each square a life I’ll never get to know;
They blink beneath the smog-stained, starless sky,
Like eyes that close when waking dreams are slow.

We tear through shadows, stitching time with speed,
The dark outside is thick as velvet cloth,
But here, inside, there’s nothing left to need—
Just rhythm, rail, and memory of growth.

The town recedes into the black unknown,
A kingdom built on sleep, yet never gone.
